   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!

Please state if there should be

From Dave Phillips, BRIDGEND



Dear Ron and Brian,

Can you inform me and,I'd guess,
quite a few of your readers via
"OUTLET" or by letter as to how
the following can be done!.

(1) To get the flashing entries
when examining BASIC listing. (I
can set it off but can not find
out how to stop it to continue
the listing without everything
else flashing).

(2) To stop the program name ob-
literating the screen when load-
ing from tape or microdrives.

(3)To set up a program in M/Code
from a "REM" statement (This has
got me completely baffled. If a
hard copy is sought from the
printer it comes out as so much
rubbish that it cannot be of any
help in trying to decipher what
is happening!). I do not really
understand much about M/Code but
have managed to alter parts of
standard programs albeit after
much head-scratching and soul-
searching. I could have just
been lucky and found a section
of BASIC embedded in the code as
all I was trying to do was to
alter the address and phone
number that was printed out by a
commercial program and also to
alter the copyright message.

(4) Is there a book or listing
that can be obtained to better
understand the locations in
"ROM" such as what happens if
RANDOMIZE USR 1000 is entered or
any other address in ROM for
that matter?.

(5)How to stop the border flash
when loading or saving programs?

Any help with the foregoing
would be appreciated or if it
has given you an idea for future
editorial material I will look
forward to seeing it in print on
the screen. In all fairness item
(3) would probably be a bit
long-winded to explain outright
but would make an ideal topic
for a few issues of OUTCLASS.

As can be deduced from my
comments on your magazine,OUTLET
is the best that I have seen for
any serious person who is
interested in making the most
use of the Spectrum memory and
not just as a games machine. I
must congratulate you both on
the first-class effort that you
give to your readership!.

             Yours sincerely,

             D.H. Phillips.

To Dave Phillips from Brian

(1) To enter colour codes into a
48K BASIC line, including FLASH,
first select EXTENDED MODE then
use the following keys...

          0 TO 7 for PAPER
  SHIFT + 0 TO 7 for INK
               8 for BRIGHT 0
               9 for BRIGHT 1
  SHIFT +      8 for FLASH  0
               9 for FLASH  1

(2) A simple method of stopping
the program name obliterating
part of the screen when loading
from tape (microdrive doesn't
print the program name) is to
set the INK colour to the same
as PAPER as in the following...

10 BORDER 5: PAPER 5: INK 1:CLS
20 PRINT TEXT, GRAPHICS ETC.
30 INK 5 (invisible on PAPER 5)
40 PRINT AT Y,0 (Y=2 less than
50 LOAD ""       any blank line)
60 INK 1  (restore INK)

The program name prints up in
"invisible ink" but still blanks
out anything (not already blank)
on the line where it prints.It's
easy with a text screen to force
the program name to print on a
blank line between paragraphs
but if there is no blank line,
e.g., in a picture, try NOCHARS
(OUTLET 25).There are other ways
such as diverting PRINT or using
special loading code but each
has advantages/disadvantages in
different situations.

(3) The easiest way to put a
machine code program into a REM
is to use REMSTORE (OUTLET 6).
(not available to +3 users who
might consider ordering the tape
version). Alternatively, try the
following...

  10 GO SUB 9940
  20 LOAD "NAME" CODE NX
  30 STOP
9940 LET NX=(PEEK 23637+256*PEEK
     23638+5): RETURN
9950 REM      rem full of number
     of spaces equal to number
     of bytes of machine code

Then delete line 10 to 20 and
alter 9940 to RANDOMIZE USR(PEEK
etc. then use GO SUB 9940 to run
the code.

You may need an LDIR and JP at
the start of your code to move
the code elsewhere in memory if
it's not relocatable that is,if
it will not run at the address
of the REM (which may move about
in memory, e.g. when a channel
is OPENed).

(4) Yes, "The Complete Spectrum
ROM Disassembly"by Dr. Ian Logan
and Dr. Frank O'hara (ISBN 0
86161 116 0)gives details of the
Spectrum ROM but you may have to
search for a copy through the
shelves of bookstores, libraries
etc. There is also the SPECTRUM
ROM INDEX which is a massive
work on the subject. Send an SAE
to Francis Miles, Windrush,
Rabley Heath, Welwyn, Herts AL6
9UF for info.

(5) The border flash that occurs
in microdrive operations can be
stopped with POKE 23750,B where
B is the current BORDER colour.
Stopping the flashing border in
tape operations needs a special
loader. This might be created by
copying the Spectrum routine to
memory and altering the colours.
I'll make a note to have a look
or perhaps BoB Smith could do an
OUTCLASS?

Hope that helps but write again
if clarification needed.


                         - Brian

To Percy Ellis from Brian

I like the idea of showing the
issue number in the editorial

of course, the header only gets
printed in TABLOID. I shall make

issue number AND data henceforth
where appropriate.Funny I didn't
think of it before actually!

To upgrade to a disc drive there
are few choices...

1. Buy a Spectrum +3. Only worth
considering if you feel you need
a new Spectrum anyway or you'd
like a 128K machine or you want

to try CP/M (system software you
can buy in addition for about
`30 which enables you to run
CP/M programs). Otherwise rather
an expensive way to switch to a
disc drive as you would pay up
to `200. What is worse, it uses
3" discs which cost about four
or five times as much to store
the same data as a 3.5" disc and
the drive can only use one side
of the 3" discs at a time.

2. Buy a SWIFTDISK interface and
drive. Fast but we've found the
company difficult to contact and
there is little support. I do
not have the price as they never
answered any of our letters but
think the system and drive is
around `140 to `160.

3. Buy a 2nd-hand Opus Discovery
(no longer available new). Good
system with a good user group
(see OUTBOARD). The standard
drive gives only 173K per disc
but the system can run 780K
drives if you are prepared to
scour the classified adverts for
a while. You could probably get
a standard drive (includes the
interface in one neat unit) for
about `70 to `90 2nd-hand. ERASE
and CAT are very, very fast.

4. Buy a Disciple or +D.Both are
compatible but the more-costly
Disciple has extra features like
networking. Both systems are
interfaces so you also need to
buy a drive or drives and these
are sold optionally with the
interface.

The systems are fast, give 780K
per 3.5" disc, reasonably well-
supported with a user group.Both
have a Centronics printer port
and a "snapshot" button (makes
it easier to save programs like
games to disc) but I don't think
the +D has a joystick port nor a
"thru-port" making it a problem
to add extra hardware (although
it can be got round).


Disciple/+D and Opus understand
microdrive syntax so will run
much of your microdrive programs
but the +3 won't.It's also worth
remembering OUTLET is available
on ALL systems but SWIFTDISK (we
tried but they didn't want to
know!)

I strongly recommend that you go
for the +D which is good value
at only `129.99 post free for
both drive and interface from
Datel Electronics Ltd., Govan
Road, Fenton Industrial Estate,
Fenton, Stoke-on-Trent, ST4 2RS
(Tel: 0782 744707). You should
feel at home since you run it
much like your microdrive but
you'll find it much faster and
much more reliable and much
cheaper for the discs (compared
to cartridges). Furthermore, the
discs are very widely available.
If you want to keep running your
microdrive then get a Disciple,
`189.95 (inc. delivery) from
MICROSNIPS, 37 Seaview Road,
Wallasey, Merseyside, L45 4QN
(Tel:051 630 3013)because it can
"piggyback" Interface 1!- Brian

From Steve Pittman



Dear Ron and Brian,

Would it be possible to get a
more detailed explanation of how
the animation works in 'DEMOPIX'
as the 'FLASH ' manual is very

To Steve Pittman from Brian

There are many ways to animate
screens but the three common
ways of doing it in SAM BASIC
are 1.colour-cycling, 2.screen
switching, 3.GRAB and PUT. FLASH
uses both colour-cycling and the
equivalent of GRAB and PUT.

Colour-cycling requires a screen
to be carefully designed that
has adjacent areas of the screen
in the next palette colour and
then the palette is switched
rapidly when the picture is
displayed. This needs a lot of
ingenuity for complex screens
but you could experiment with
simple vertical or horizontal
coloured bars like a test card.

Try the following to see how
this is done in FLASH...

Load FLASH and then load"bugsS$"
from Issue 35.Notice the circles
in the background are colours in
sequence from 9 to 14.Two of the
numbers from 0 to 15 above the
palette colours are highlighted
in green. These may already by
9 and 14 but, if not, move the
cursor over 9 and press N and
over 14 and press M. They should
now be green. You can't move the
N selection higher than the M
and vice versa so you may need
to move the M selection first
(e.g., if M were set at 5 and N
at 8 you could not move M to 9
until you first move N to 14,
geddit?).

Now, move the cursor over the
left "C" of"CYC" in the top left
corner.Press "M" (or FIRE on a
joystick)and the colours between
9 and 14 switch with their
neighbouring colour to the right
and the coloured rings appear to
move outward. If you keep press-
ing then you will see the
colours seem to "flow" outwards.
The other C of CYC moves them
the other way.

If you move the cursor over the
+ or - below CYC and press N or
M you will see the 0 between
change and the colours will now
switch continuously at varying
rates. Experiment with the + and
- to see this. Get it back to 0
to stop it.

To do the same thing from BASIC,
you need to POKE the PALETTE
table thus (for the six colours
used in the bugs bunny example):

POKE 21985, CHR$ PEEK 21991 +
MEM$(21985 TO 21990):
POKE 22005, CHR$ PEEK 22011 +
MEM$(22005 TO 22010)

      ...which move each palette
value along one address and puts
the last one at the start.

The complete 16-colour palette
values are stored in memory in
two sequences (identical unless
you have set flashing colours
using e.g. PALETTE 4,55,99) from
21976 to 21991 and from 21996 to
22011. Both sequences have to be
POKED.

Screen switching in BASIC needs
a series of full screens each
slightly different (like movie
film)and shown in rapid sequence
using SCREEN (see the SAM user
manual).

With PUT and GRAB you would make
a sequential series of images
(like movie film) on just parts
of the screen and GRAB each
"frame" and PUT them all in fast
succession at the same place on
the screen.

The FLASH equivalent is best
described by example and Stephen
Wilson has kindly sent in the
screen of frames used to create
the KINGANI demo.His explanation
follows...

"Load the screen "KINGANI.S"from
this issue into FLASH!. Select
the animation icon [looks like a
piece of movie film].


Go to the 'F' box and select the
> on it.

A box will appear as if you are
cutting a block. Just put the
box over the first frame and
select it.


Do this 6 times for each frame
and then advance the > arrow at
the 'E' box until it reaches 6
and then select any green patch
in the animation section and it
should animate.

If you're getting frame wobbling
you must have not marked each
frame as the same size. You must
put the box over each white
outline put over each frame."
   - courtesy of Stephen Wilson

Ignore the'MARK' box which shows
how many frames have been made -
use it only when you want to re-
do a frame already used (alter F
first to the frame you want then
select "MARK")."S" alters speed;
B and E the beginning and end
frames used in the animation.

Technical manuals are available
for `15.99 from SAM COMPUTERS
LTD., 7 Clevedon Court, Uplands,
Swansea, SA2 0RG

Hope that helps.        - Brian

To Dave Phillips from Brian

(1) To enter colour codes into a 48K BASIC line, including FLASH, first select EXTENDED MODE then use the following keys...

0 TO 7 for PAPER SHIFT + 0 TO 7 for INK 8 for BRIGHT 0 9 for BRIGHT 1 SHIFT +      8 for FLASH  0 9 for FLASH  1

(2) A simple method of stopping the program name obliterating part of the screen when loading from tape (microdrive doesn't print the program name) is to set the INK colour to the same as PAPER as in the following...

10 BORDER 5: PAPER 5: INK 1:CLS 20 PRINT TEXT, GRAPHICS ETC. 30 INK 5 (invisible on PAPER 5) 40 PRINT AT Y,0 (Y=2 less than 50 LOAD ""       any blank line) 60 INK 1  (restore INK)

The program name prints up in "invisible ink" but still blanks out anything (not already blank) on the line where it prints.It's easy with a text screen to force the program name to print on a blank line between paragraphs but if there is no blank line, e.g., in a picture, try NOCHARS (OUTLET 25).There are other ways such as diverting PRINT or using special loading code but each has advantages/disadvantages in different situations.

(3) The easiest way to put a machine code program into a REM is to use REMSTORE (OUTLET 6). (not available to +3 users who might consider ordering the tape version). Alternatively, try the following...

10 GO SUB 9940 20 LOAD "NAME" CODE NX 30 STOP 9940 LET NX=(PEEK 23637+256*PEEK 23638+5): RETURN 9950 REM      rem full of number of spaces equal to number of bytes of machine code

Then delete line 10 to 20 and alter 9940 to RANDOMIZE USR(PEEK etc. then use GO SUB 9940 to run the code.

You may need an LDIR and JP at the start of your code to move the code elsewhere in memory if it's not relocatable that is,if it will not run at the address of the REM (which may move about in memory, e.g. when a channel is OPENed).

To Steve Pittman from Brian

There are many ways to animate screens but the three common ways of doing it in SAM BASIC are 1.colour-cycling, 2.screen switching, 3.GRAB and PUT. FLASH uses both colour-cycling and the equivalent of GRAB and PUT.

Colour-cycling requires a screen to be carefully designed that has adjacent areas of the screen in the next palette colour and then the palette is switched rapidly when the picture is displayed. This needs a lot of ingenuity for complex screens but you could experiment with simple vertical or horizontal coloured bars like a test card.

Try the following to see how this is done in FLASH...

Load FLASH and then load"bugsS$" from Issue 35.Notice the circles in the background are colours in sequence from 9 to 14.Two of the numbers from 0 to 15 above the palette colours are highlighted in green. These may already by 9 and 14 but, if not, move the cursor over 9 and press N and over 14 and press M. They should now be green. You can't move the N selection higher than the M and vice versa so you may need to move the M selection first (e.g., if M were set at 5 and N at 8 you could not move M to 9 until you first move N to 14, geddit?).

Now, move the cursor over the left "C" of"CYC" in the top left corner.Press "M" (or FIRE on a joystick)and the colours between 9 and 14 switch with their neighbouring colour to the right and the coloured rings appear to move outward. If you keep press- ing then you will see the colours seem to "flow" outwards. The other C of CYC moves them the other way.

If you move the cursor over the + or - below CYC and press N or M you will see the 0 between change and the colours will now switch continuously at varying rates. Experiment with the + and - to see this. Get it back to 0 to stop it.

To do the same thing from BASIC, you need to POKE the PALETTE table thus (for the six colours used in the bugs bunny example):

POKE 21985, CHR$ PEEK 21991 + MEM$(21985 TO 21990): POKE 22005, CHR$ PEEK 22011 + MEM$(22005 TO 22010)

...which move each palette value along one address and puts the last one at the start.

The complete 16-colour palette values are stored in memory in two sequences (identical unless you have set flashing colours using e.g. PALETTE 4,55,99) from 21976 to 21991 and from 21996 to 22011. Both sequences have to be POKED.

Screen switching in BASIC needs a series of full screens each slightly different (like movie film)and shown in rapid sequence using SCREEN (see the SAM user manual).

With PUT and GRAB you would make a sequential series of images (like movie film) on just parts of the screen and GRAB each "frame" and PUT them all in fast succession at the same place on the screen.

The FLASH equivalent is best described by example and Stephen Wilson has kindly sent in the screen of frames used to create the KINGANI demo.His explanation follows...

"Load the screen "KINGANI.S"from this issue into FLASH!. Select the animation icon [looks like a piece of movie film].

Go to the 'F' box and select the > on it.

A box will appear as if you are cutting a block. Just put the box over the first frame and select it.

Do this 6 times for each frame and then advance the > arrow at the 'E' box until it reaches 6 and then select any green patch in the animation section and it should animate.

If you're getting frame wobbling you must have not marked each frame as the same size. You must put the box over each white outline put over each frame." - courtesy of Stephen Wilson

Ignore the'MARK' box which shows how many frames have been made - use it only when you want to re- do a frame already used (alter F first to the frame you want then select "MARK")."S" alters speed; B and E the beginning and end frames used in the animation.

Technical manuals are available for `15.99 from SAM COMPUTERS LTD., 7 Clevedon Court, Uplands, Swansea, SA2 0RG

### От Dave Phillips, BRIDGEND

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Не могли бы вы рассказать мне и, полагаю, многим вашим читателям через «OUTLET» или в письме, как сделать следующее?

(3) Как запустить программу в машинных кодах из оператора «REM»? (Это меня совершенно сбило с толку. Если вывести копию на принтер, получается такая абракадабра, что она ничем не помогает понять, что происходит!). ### Ответ для Dave Phillips от Brian

(1) Чтобы ввести цветовые коды в строку 48K BASIC, включая FLASH, сначала выберите EXTENDED MODE, а затем используйте следующие клавиши:

```text
         0 ДО 7 для PAPER
 SHIFT + 0 ДО 7 для INK
              8 для BRIGHT 0
              9 для BRIGHT 1
 SHIFT +      8 для FLASH  0
              9 для FLASH  1
```

(2) Простой способ предотвратить затирание части экрана именем программы при загрузке с ленты (микродрайв не печатает имя программы) — это установить цвет INK таким же, как PAPER, как в следующем примере:

```text
10 BORDER 5: PAPER 5: INK 1: CLS
20 PRINT TEXT, GRAPHICS ETC.
30 INK 5 (невидим на PAPER 5)
40 PRINT AT Y,0 (Y на 2 меньше любой пустой строки)
50 LOAD ""
60 INK 1 (восстанавливаем INK)
```

Имя программы печатается «невидимыми чернилами», но все равно стирает всё (что еще не пусто) на строке, где оно выводится. На текстовом экране легко заставить имя программы напечататься на пустой строке между абзацами, но если пустой строки нет (например, на картинке), попробуйте NOCHARS (OUTLET 25). Есть и другие способы, такие как перенаправление PRINT или использование специального загрузчика в кодах, но у каждого есть свои преимущества и недостатки в различных ситуациях.

(3) Самый простой способ поместить программу в машинных кодах в REM — использовать REMSTORE (OUTLET 6) (недоступно пользователям +3, которым стоит подумать о заказе версии на кассете). В качестве альтернативы попробуйте следующее:

```text
  10 GO SUB 9940
  20 LOAD "NAME" CODE NX
  30 STOP
9940 LET NX=(PEEK 23637+256*PEEK 23638+5): RETURN
9950 REM      rem, заполненный пробелами в количестве,
              равном числу байт машинного кода
```

Затем удалите строки с 10 по 20 и измените 9940 на RANDOMIZE USR(PEEK и т.д., после чего используйте GO SUB 9940 для запуска кода.

Возможно, вам понадобятся команды LDIR и JP в начале вашего кода, чтобы переместить его в другую область памяти, если он не перемещаемый (то есть, если он не может выполняться прямо по адресу REM, который может сдвигаться в памяти, например, при открытии канала — OPEN).

(4) Да, книга «The Complete Spectrum ROM Disassembly» доктора Ian Logan и доктора Frank O'Hara (ISBN 0 86161 116 0) дает подробное описание ROM Спектрума, но вам, возможно, придется поискать экземпляр на полках книжных магазинов, библиотек и т.д. Существует также SPECTRUM ROM INDEX — монументальный труд на эту тему. Отправьте конверт с маркой и обратным адресом (SAE) по адресу: Francis Miles, Windrush, Rabley Heath, Welwyn, Herts AL6 9UF для получения информации.

(5) Мигание бордюра, возникающее при работе с микродрайвом, можно отключить с помощью POKE 23750,B, где B — текущий цвет BORDER. 1. Купить Spectrum +3. Этот вариант стоит рассматривать только в том случае, если вам в любом случае нужен новый Спектрум, или вы хотите 128K машину, или хотите...

### Steve Pittman от Brian

Существует множество способов анимировать изображение, но три самых распространённых в SAM BASIC — это:
1. Циклический сдвиг цветов (colour-cycling);
2. Переключение экранов;
3. GRAB и PUT.

FLASH использует как циклический сдвиг цветов, так и аналог GRAB и PUT.

Цветовой циклинг требует тщательно продуманного экрана, где соседние области окрашены в следующие по порядку цвета палитры, а затем при показе картинки палитра быстро переключается. Для сложных картинок здесь требуется немалая изобретательность, но вы можете поэкспериментировать с простыми вертикальными или горизонтальными цветными полосами, как на настроечной таблице.

Попробуйте сделать следующее, чтобы увидеть, как это работает в FLASH...

Загрузите FLASH, а затем загрузите «bugsS$» из 35-го номера. Обратите внимание, что круги на фоне раскрашены последовательностью цветов от 9 до 14. Две цифры от 0 до 15 над цветами палитры подсвечены зелёным. Возможно, это уже 9 и 14, но если нет — наведите курсор на 9 и нажмите N, а затем на 14 и нажмите M. Теперь они должны стать зелёными. Вы не можете переместить маркер N выше маркера M и наоборот, поэтому, возможно, сначала придётся подвинуть маркер M (например, если M стоял на 5, а N на 8, вы не сможете сдвинуть M на 9, пока сначала не переставите N на 14, сечёте?).

Теперь наведите курсор на левую букву «C» в надписи «CYC» в верхнем левом углу. Нажмите «M» (или FIRE на джойстике) — цвета между 9 и 14 поменяются местами с соседними цветами справа, и покажется, будто цветные кольца движутся наружу. Если продолжать нажимать, вы увидите, как цвета словно «перетекают» вовне. Вторая буква «C» в слове «CYC» сдвигает их в обратную сторону.

Если навести курсор на «+» или «-» под надписью CYC и нажать N или M, вы увидите, как меняется ноль между ними, и цвета начнут переключаться непрерывно с разной скоростью. Поэкспериментируйте с «+» и «-», чтобы увидеть это в действии. Верните значение на 0, чтобы остановить процесс.

Чтобы сделать то же самое из BASIC, вам нужно записать значения через POKE в таблицу PALETTE следующим образом (для шести цветов, использованных в примере с Bugs Bunny):

```text
POKE 21985, CHR$ PEEK 21991 + MEM$(21985 TO 21990):
POKE 22005, CHR$ PEEK 22011 + MEM$(22005 TO 22010)
```

...что сдвигает каждое значение палитры на один адрес вперёд, а последнее помещает в начало.

Полные значения 16-цветной палитры хранятся в памяти в двух последовательностях (одинаковых, если только вы не настроили мигающие цвета с помощью, например, `PALETTE 4,55,99`) от 21976 до 21991 и от 21996 до 22011. Обе последовательности необходимо изменять через POKE.

Переключение экранов в BASIC требует серии полных экранов, каждый из которых слегка отличается от предыдущего (как на киноплёнке), и быстрой их смены при помощи команды SCREEN (см. руководство пользователя SAM).

С помощью PUT и GRAB вы создаёте последовательную серию кадров (как на киноплёнке) лишь на отдельных участках экрана, «захватываете» каждый кадр командой GRAB и быстро выводите их все командой PUT в одно и то же место экрана один за другим.

Аналог этого во FLASH лучше всего описать на примере, и Stephen Wilson любезно прислал экран с кадрами, использованными для создания демо KINGANI. Вот его объяснение...

«Загрузите экран "KINGANI.S" из этого номера во FLASH!. Выберите значок анимации [похож на кусочек киноплёнки].

Перейдите к блоку 'F' и нажмите стрелку > на нём.

Появится рамка, как при вырезании блока. Просто наведите эту рамку на первый кадр и выберите его.

Повторите это 6 раз для каждого кадра, а затем щёлкайте по стрелке > у блока 'E', пока значение не достигнет 6, после чего нажмите на любую зелёную область в секции анимации — картинка должна ожить.

Если кадры "пляшут", значит, вы выделили кадры разного размера. Рамку необходимо накладывать точно по белым контурам, нарисованным вокруг каждого кадра».
— любезно предоставлено Stephen Wilson

Не обращайте внимания на поле 'MARK', которое показывает количество созданных кадров — используйте его только тогда, когда хотите переделать уже задействованный кадр (сначала измените значение F на номер нужного кадра, затем выберите «MARK»). «S» меняет скорость; B и E — начальный и конечный кадры анимации.

Technical manuals можно приобрести за £15.99 в SAM COMPUTERS LTD., 7 Clevedon Court, Uplands, Swansea, SA2 0RG.

Надеюсь, это поможет.

— Brian
